body_text:
For a predicate $P(x)$ on a domain $D$, the existential
statement $\exists x\in D\,P(x)$ is true exactly when at least
one $a\in D$ satisfies $P(a)$. Such an $a$ is called a witness.
An existence proof must establish both that the proposed
witness belongs to the domain and that it satisfies the
predicate; uniqueness is a separate assertion.
